title: One-step antimicrobial peptide immobilization technique: universal compatibility with clinical bone cements
content: Nisin-based antimicrobial peptide (AMP) immobilization represents a promising strategy for antibacterial bone cements. This one-step approach fits standard surgical workflows and addresses drawbacks of antibiotic-loaded cements, such as burst drug release, short-term antibacterial activity and compromised mechanical properties. Nevertheless, its compatibility with clinical cements for translation has not been verified. Here, we covalently anchored nisin onto three clinical cements during in situ polymerization and assessed pre-clinical performances. The modified cements maintained ISO-compliant compressive strength and MMA release profiles remained largely unaltered. They yielded 94–100% contact-killing efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus without peptide leaching. Moreover, the treated cements maintained desirable handling properties and biocompatibility. This work validates the broad compatibility of this one-step technique. Featuring low-cost nisin, it offers an accessible translational anti-infective cement strategy, especially for resource-limited regions.
